analysis: What changed vs the 8 AM brief: the slide accelerated again into the late morning — the Nasdaq went from -1.8% to -2.9% at its session low, the S&P from -0.7% to -1.5%, and the S&P has now slipped below Thursday's 7,173.63 intraday low, while the Dow clings to flat. Anthropic is down another leg to just above $87, roughly $4 from the $83 IPO price after an $85.66 intraday low, and the IPO is now confirmed to have raised $93.5B including the greenshoe — the 'IPO as top' read is no longer a take, it's the tape. The chip rout widened into memory: Sandisk -13% on its first post-split day (quote software briefly showed -89%, per WSB), Micron/Seagate/Western Digital -10%+, AMD -8-10%, SMH -7.5%. The one genuine divergence is Alphabet, +2.4% and the only green Mag 7 name, on the same day it issued a C$6B bond in Canada — money is picking a winner inside the AI trade rather than buying the whole complex. The Dow's flat print is still rotation, not strength: IBM, Travelers, Walmart and Gilead lead while tech liquidates. Overnight Asia was ugly (Taiex -6.75%, Kospi -5.7%, Nikkei -4.8%), and the WSB daily thread's fear/greed read is ~10/100, extreme fear, with the community treating $83 as the line in the sand for a market-wide flush. Signal vs noise: the seventh-day slide, NVDA making new lows, ANT approaching $83, the S&P under Thursday's low and its 200-day, and the VIX spiking above 31 premarket are signal; the Dow's flat print and Alphabet's green day are rotation; Michigan's inflation-expectations plunge remains signal for the December Fed path even though the tape ignored it. The close now hinges on whether ANT holds $83, whether monthly options expiration pins or flushes the tape, and what Fed Governors Cook and Waller say this afternoon.

headlines.headline: Selloff accelerates into the late morning: Nasdaq -2.9% at its session low, S&P 500 -1.5%, Dow flat (IBD, ~8:55 AM PT). Seventh straight down day; the Nasdaq briefly slipped into negative territory for 2026 (Investopedia), and the S&P has now fallen below Thursday's 7,173.63 intraday low. Indexes are on track for their worst week since early last year — S&P and Dow down ~5% on the week, Nasdaq down more than 6%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The slide is deepening into the session rather than stabilizing — and the Dow's flat print is rotation into defensives, not broad strength.

headlines.headline: Anthropic (ANT) down more than 10% to just above $87 (IBD), with an intraday low of $85.66 (WSB analysis, 10:35 AM ET) — roughly $4 above the $83 IPO price. The company confirmed the IPO raised $93.5 billion including the greenshoe on 1.127 billion shares. It closed Thursday at $97.17 after debuting at $111.50.
headlines.why_it_matters: Day two is now testing the IPO price itself — a break of $83 hardens the 'IPO as top' read and removes the AI trade's last floor.

headlines.headline: Chip and memory rout widens: Nvidia (NVDA) -6% to ~$138, new lows well below Thursday's $145.71 52-week low. Sandisk -13% on its first day after an 8-for-1 split; Micron, Seagate and Western Digital -10% to -10.5%; AMD -8% to -10%; Broadcom and Marvell -9%+. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) is down 7.5%, SOXX -6%, memory ETF DRAM -8%. Data-center names CoreWeave and Nebius -9%. (IBD, Investopedia)
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is now a liquidation of the whole AI hardware chain, not just Nvidia — breadth inside tech is uniformly red, which is what makes the tape hard to stabilize. The record Q3 (EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B) is not stopping the slide.

headlines.headline: Alphabet (GOOGL) +2.4% — the only green Mag 7 name — on the same day Alphabet issued a C$6 billion (about US$4.19 billion) bond in Canada (WSB analysis). Apple is roughly flat to lower, while Meta is down more than 3% and Amazon, Microsoft and Tesla are also lower (Investopedia, WSB analysis).
headlines.why_it_matters: Money is picking a winner inside the AI trade rather than buying the whole complex — Alphabet holding up while the rest of the Mag 7 sinks is the clearest rotation signal of the morning.

headlines.headline: Tesla (TSLA) upgraded by HSBC to Hold from Reduce today (MarketBeat, 11/20/2026), but shares are still lower with the tape. (Investopedia)
headlines.why_it_matters: An upgrade on a day the whole tape is red shows how little single-name news matters right now — the move is macro and sector-driven, not stock-specific.

headlines.headline: Defensive rotation continues: IBM +3% and Travelers +3% lead the Dow, Walmart +3% after Thursday's earnings, Gilead +1.5%, Keurig Dr Pepper +2%; health insurers remain strong after Thursday's TD Cowen upgrades (Humana +5%, UnitedHealth +3%). Earnings movers: Ross Stores -6%, BJ's Wholesale -6%, Elastic -3%. (IBD)
headlines.why_it_matters: Money is rotating, not just leaving — defensives and a few earnings winners are absorbing flows, which is why the Dow is flat while the Nasdaq sinks.

headlines.headline: 10-year Treasury yield down 11 bps to 4.94% — its fourth straight daily decline from the 5.05% Thursday close — as safe-haven buying continues. The VIX is at 29.50, up 1.08 points, after touching 30.04 and spiking above 31 in premarket (Reuters). Gold futures down 3.6% to $3,555, their lowest since September 2025; WTI crude $82.35, down 1.1%; Bitcoin near $62,000. December Fed hike pricing sits at ~96% for a 25bp hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting. (IBD, Reuters, Investopedia, Barchart)
headlines.why_it_matters: Yields falling while hike odds stay near-certain is the tension in the tape — bonds are pricing safety, not a Fed pivot, and gold's 3.6% drop shows even havens are being sold for liquidity.

headlines.headline: Overnight Asia sold off hard: Taiwan's Taiex -6.75%, Korea's Kospi -5.7%, Japan's Nikkei -4.8% (WSB analysis). Breadth in the US: Nasdaq decliners beat advancers by about 2-to-1, and NYSE losers beat winners by about 14 to 11 (IBD).
headlines.why_it_matters: The unwind is global, not a US-only wobble — Asia's overnight rout set the tone for the morning, and US breadth confirms sellers are in control across the board.
